chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Aslam from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (peace be upon them both): I arrived in al-Kūfah and had not fasted the seven days, until I was hurried on a need to Baghdād. He said, 'Fast them in Baghdād.' I said, 'Shall I distribute them?' He said, 'Yes.'

And whoever missed the fasting of these three days in Makkah due to an impediment hindering him or forgetfulness overtaking him, let him fast them on the road if he wishes, and if he wishes to fast them when he returns to his family, that is permissible for him. Narrated.
ai.seo_question: How to make up missed voluntary fasting days due to travel or forgetfulness?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies the flexibility in compensating for the missed seven days of voluntary fasting (Sawm al-Wafada) due to travel or impediments, explicitly permitting the fasts to be performed non-consecutively and at the traveler's convenience. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of ease (Yusr) in voluntary acts, distinguishing them from obligatory make-up fasts which often require immediate succession. The ruling underscores the importance of maintaining spiritual discipline even when circumstances prevent immediate observance upon arrival in Mecca.
